ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Cinder.cs:22-25) == cost 2 / ATTACK / COMMON / ANY_ENEMY. Cinder has NO Exhaust keyword of its own -- the Exhaust hover tip (Cinder.cs:20) refers to the hand card it exhausts -- and the sim correctly leaves `exhausts` False.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(18m, ValueProp.Move)` (Cinder.cs:18) == `_damage = 18`, powered on both sides.

OnPlay.rationale: Order matches: attack FIRST (Cinder.cs:30-33), then exhaust a random hand card (34-39). The RNG is handled correctly here, unlike anointed/beat_down: `Rng.CombatCardSelection.NextItem(pile.Cards)` (Cinder.cs:35) maps to `crng.card_selection.choice(ctx.player.hand)` under parity, with the shared legacy rng only in the non-parity branch (cinder.py:40-44) -- the pattern the other 20 shared-rng cards should follow. The empty-hand case matches (`if (cardModel != null)` == `if ctx.player.hand:`). Cinder itself is never a candidate: C# holds it in the Play pile, the sim in the discard-pile limbo (combat.py:452-454). Presentation, folded in: WithAttackerAnim's Ironclad heavy-anim helpers and the NFireBurstVfx hit node.

guards.what: the hand is read AFTER the attack resolves, so a card added to hand by the attack is a candidate
guards.rationale: Both sides fetch the hand at the exhaust step, not before the attack. Same candidate set.
